title: Direct synthesis of a tetranuclear erbium(III) hydroxo cluster bearing a saturated Schiff base

synthesis.procedure: Under N2/Schlenk and glovebox conditions, a 100 mL Schlenk flask was charged with 0.790 g (1.21 mmol) tris(bis(trimethylsilyl)amido)erbium and 10 mL heptane, sealed, removed from the glovebox, and interfaced to a Schlenk line. In a separate flask, 0.426 g (1.21 mmol) ligand 2 was dissolved in 60 mL heptane with gentle warming and added to the erbium flask in two 30 mL aliquots by syringe. Under flowing N2 a condenser was fitted and the mixture was refluxed for 12 h. The homogeneous orange-pink mother liquor was concentrated in vacuo to about 10 mL and cooled to -10 °C. Light pink crystals of 3 were harvested after 4 days.
synthesis.time: reflux 12 h; crystals harvested after 4 days
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Schlenk flask / silylamide route under flowing N2
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: concentrated in vacuo to ~10 mL and cooled to -10 °C; light pink crystals harvested after 4 days

synthesis.procedure: Following the 12 h reflux used to generate 3 in situ from 0.790 g (1.21 mmol) Er[N(SiMe3)2]3 and 0.426 g (1.21 mmol) ligand 2 in heptane, 1.1 equiv H2O was added as a freshly prepared, degassed C7H16:H2O azeotrope (0.16 mL). The solution was stirred and heated at 30–35 °C overnight, concentrated in vacuo to about 6 mL, and light-yellow crystals of 4 were obtained after 2.5 days. The same Er4(OH)4 core was also accessible by sequential hydrolysis of isolated 3 using stoichiometric or modest excess water.

reagents.name: tris(bis(trimethylsilyl)amido)erbium
reagents.amount: 0.790 g (1.21 mmol) as in the procedure for 3

reagents.name: bis-5,5'-(2,2-dimethyl-1,3-propanediyldiimino)-2,2-dimethyl-4-hexen-3-one (2)
reagents.amount: 0.426 g (1.21 mmol) as in the procedure for 3

reagents.name: water
reagents.amount: 1.1 equiv as 0.16 mL degassed C7H16:H2O azeotrope

synthesis.vessel_or_method: in situ hydrolysis of 3 under Schlenk/N2 conditions
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: orange solution concentrated in vacuo to ~6 mL; light-yellow crystals obtained after 2.5 days
